Section: Materials Lab v1 > Browse and inspect actual behaviour
Search by exact stable ID, name, physical state, kernel, semantic family or reaction partner. Filters include physical states and explicit hard/granular capabilities. These categories organize the browser; neither appearance labels nor semantic family membership confer inherited physics. Every important property row separates **declared value → effective value → actual consumer → applicability → editability**. The native cold-path bridge reads original descriptor values, capability predicates, density-exchange eligibility, visual-state projection and compiled solver defaults. The model also consumes the existing native interaction profile. Missing native support fails explicitly. It never substitutes shadow catalogue values for native facts. Examples to check: - **Water:** the specialised Water family determines motion. Descriptor viscosity is not a Lab edit. CellularYield Water's versioned policy viscosity is a separate consumer; it is not the descriptor viscosity byte. - **Sand:** powder movement, density and explicit hard/granular capabilities are separate facts. A powder name never implies hard terrain. - **Slush:** native density is 1080; the separately identified GDScript fallback has density 1100. Neither value is silently substituted for the other. - **MoltenGlass:** yielding movement and specialised thermal behaviour are shown separately, including the actual consumers and the admitted descriptor fields. - **Lava, Acid and Oil:** an ignored descriptor viscosity is labelled ineffective for the specialised kernel, and the candidate control is disabled. When opened from Shared Workbench, the inspector receives a **copied applied policy receipt at opening**. Reopen to refresh it. A standalone Lab labels compiled defaults as unobserved by a live World. **Inspect test-owner policy** switches the inspector to the isolated experiment's acknowledged native policy. The UI never reads a simulation-worker-owned World from the main thread. Sources: [native inspection](../../godot/native_extension/material_lab_inspection.inc), [catalogue model](../../godot/scripts/material_lab_catalogue.gd), [panel](../../godot/scripts/material_lab_panel.gd) and the minimal [Workbench mount](../../godot/scripts/shared_workbench.gd).

Section: Canonical material catalogue and interaction authoring — adopted Planned baseline > 5. Interaction effects and effective parameters > Effective parameter contract
`MaterialDefinition.viscosity_index` is a **declared** value; effective motion depends on kernel and any allowed construction-time profiles. Every proposed editable parameter needs: - stable key; declared and effective values; units and validated limits; - owning source/preset/override and identity/version of the applied policy; - **actual consuming kernel/helper** and supported platform/solver; - status `effective`, `unused_by_selected_kernel`, `unsupported`, `planned` or `source_edit_required`; - change class: appearance preview, compile/rebuild, or validated restart-time policy; - revalidation tags, state/quantity impact and save/physical-hash implications. In v1, **do not** present Lava/Acid/Oil descriptor viscosity as an effective freely editable native slider while their specialised paths bypass that value. An inspector can truthfully display the descriptor and an applicability warning. Similarly, do not infer real-world density units from `density`: it is a gameplay comparison value.

Section: Materials Lab v1 > Supported candidate edits and state transitions
Select a valid, nonempty material and **Duplicate selected**, or choose **New powder 132**. The original template selects the existing kernel and state contract. The candidate label is not a production rename. Existing IDs, enum encodings and rule slots remain fixed. | Property | Lab v1 boundary | |---|---| | Density; base RGBA | Editable candidate fields; consumed by the descriptor probe and isolated compiled World | | Explicit hard/granular capability; visual-state projection | Editable and exercised by the descriptor probe; edits are rejected by the World backend because it retains the native capability/projection consumers | | Descriptor viscosity | Editable only for generic YieldingLiquid, Cement and MoltenGlass templates; ineffective specialised-kernel edits are rejected | | Physical state, kernel, movement flags, density-motion mode, exchange permission, lateral-flow descriptor, initial state bytes and write radius | Held to the selected template; choose another template for a different admitted mechanism | | Existing sparse reaction slots owned by the template | Structured partners, products, match mode and inclusive probability threshold are editable; identity, slot and supported endpoint-effect semantics stay fixed | | Explicit endpoint effects v2 | Non-Water `keep_existing`, or declared Metal/Combustible `state_b` updates, execute only in isolated compiled Worlds; see the reaction contract below | | New arbitrary production IDs, new kernels, unknown fields, Water retention/quantity effects, arbitrary state writes, new pair-rule slots | Unsupported and rejected with a field path and explanation | | Existing Water default/FreeMass/CellularYield selection in **Native test** | Applied through existing native admission to the isolated test World, with owner readback; does not reconfigure the shared running Workbench | | Empty 0 and reserved invalid 10 | Inspectable, not candidate templates | **Draft** means editable, unqualified data. **Validated candidate** means the strict schema and immutable compatibility check passed. **Compiled/tested** means that exact candidate compiled and ran in the stated native probe. **Runtime-active** requires an authoritative production installation and engine acknowledgement; Lab v1 never assigns this state to a candidate. An edit revokes previous validation. A background response for an older revision cannot qualify newer edits. Candidate World results also bind the exact test recipe; changing seed, placement, partner, tick count or workers retires the displayed comparison. Validation refuses invalid IDs/types, duplicate JSON keys, duplicate slots, unknown or conflicting definitions, invalid/inactive reaction sources, malformed presets, unsupported state/effects and source drift. It uses the frozen compatibility lock without refreshing it. No failure publishes a partial bundle.

Section: Materials Lab v1 > Save, import, compile and compare
**Save / export preset…** writes a version-1 JSON envelope containing the exact candidate, source catalogue digest and deterministic candidate SHA-256. **Import preset…** verifies the envelope, digest, schema, current compatibility and source identity before replacing the displayed candidate. Tampered or malformed imports preserve the current candidate. The file is reusable with the same admitted source; it is not a saved World. **Compile + native test** generates the complete expanded candidate catalogue, C++ definitions and Godot metadata in a temporary external build, compiles the native probe, executes it and displays a receipt. **Export compiled bundle…** performs the same operation and saves to a fresh child directory outside the repository. The bundle contains the preset, generated files and source-bound receipt for review. Import the bundle's `preset.json` to reopen its candidate; the temporary executable is deliberately not exported. It records the compiler/version and hashes of native source inputs, generated files and the probe executable; native source identity is checked before and after compilation. The probe consumes the generated descriptor/capability/appearance values and uses the actual native sparse pair resolver over all 256 byte rolls and every unique directed pair in the union of production and candidate rules. Removed pairs remain in the comparison; self-pairs and opposite ordered rules are not double-counted. It records changed outcomes, deterministic example rolls and positional products. It reports the generated product descriptors' initial state bytes. **It does not execute World's endpoint/Water-quantity initialization, install a candidate in World, simulate candidate movement or establish quantity conservation over time.** The separate **Candidate test** backend below supplies that bounded World execution. Authoring runs in a polled child process with **Cancel authoring**, bounded output and a five-minute desktop wall limit. **Cancel World test** uses the same cancellation marker. The compiler/probe process tree is terminated on timeout or cancellation; cancelled/failed jobs cannot qualify a candidate. Closing gives cleanup at most two seconds before terminating an unresponsive process. These process controls use a private Windows Job Object established before the child executes, or a POSIX process group. Descendants are retired even if their driver already exited or redirected its streams. Four actual descendant-lifetime fixtures run on both platforms; their platform-qualified results belong to the completion record. CLI request/response paths cannot overwrite a preset or a compiled bundle through response-path aliasing.

Section: Materials Lab v1 > Native simulation experiments and reproducible cases > Inspect an actual native contact
Left-click the native preview to select a source cell and right-click to select a target. **Swap endpoints** tests the opposite source orientation. Set a byte roll and press **Inspect contact**; this pauses the exclusive test owner and copies both native cells from the same completed tick. Inspection never executes a reaction. Stored material, visible material, state A/B, raw stored temperature, body-mask identity, compiled kernel and pair capability remain separate facts. The report combines the real sparse resolver with observed neighbour distance, mask and selected source-core window facts. It also shows the preceding completed tick's applied window; that value is unobserved before the first tick. A target outside the selected core range is not automatically excluded, because contacts can reach the source core's write halo. A selected supplied roll cannot prove next-tick execution: per-cell sleeping, future wake deadlines, cell epochs, actual task dispatch, random bytes and competing neighbours remain explicitly unobserved. Editing coordinates/roll or advancing the owner retires the report. For a deterministic probability example, inspect adjacent native **Steam/Ice** cells with rolls **32** and **33**. The compiled threshold32 rule selects the reaction on32 and rejects33. The separate eligibility section explains any observed blocker without presenting the supplied roll as World's random stream. For a repeatable example, select **Salt 23 + Water 3**, seed 2, 120 ticks and four workers. Native readback observes the 384-cell Salt dose reacting with Water to produce **768 Brine cells**, with Water remaining in the bay. **Repeat / compare reference** reconstructs a clean owner with the same definition and checks exact final readback. Replay advances one tick per UI frame; **Pause** cancels it while preserving the source run. **Save test case…** records the definition, source identity, seed, worker count and applied Water-family selection in a digested envelope; **Import test case…** restores that configuration and its visible seed/duration/worker/policy controls transactionally. Prepared-run identity is shown separately from controls for a new pair. Native source or digest mismatches are refused. This is reproducible fixture reconstruction, not arbitrary World continuation or a save-format migration. Source: [experiment helper](../../godot/scripts/material_lab_experiment.gd). The previous [1024² manual laboratory](../MATERIAL_LAB.md) and the existing [MicroScenario reference pack](microscenario-reference-pack.md) retain their separate controls and evidence.

**Current, MAT-001 / #158:** after ordinary source admission and kernel execution, World checks an unchanged source for a possible compact-pair reaction, or Ice for hot/Water neighbors. A registered pair schedules its next four-tick contact lane. Ice schedules its next four-tick melting lane when heat is present, otherwise its sixteen-tick freezing sample when Water is present. All use the original stable coordinate phases. Products, probabilities, neighbor order and random streams are unchanged; the repair preserves opportunities that quiet-block sleep used to lose. A failed probability roll or an Ice sample that misses the eligible neighbor retains another opportunity. A successful neighbor-only write also rechecks the unchanged source, which matters when another contact remains across a block/core boundary. Eligibility respects body masks. Removing a mask wakes the affected resident block so its newly visible contacts can be reconsidered. This does not force a reaction on every contact or prescribe a universal completion time. Section: Activity, dirty regions, and waking > What wakes a region?
Direct `set`/`write_cell` operations mark their cells dirty and active. `wake_cell_neighborhood` wakes resident nonempty neighbors when the changed coordinate lies at an activity-block edge or corner. Movement marks both source and destination. The phased `merge_job_effects` path additionally wakes through the corners of touched block bounds, so its wake can be broader than one direct cell write. Explosion edits and transient-obstacle changes use explicit wake paths. A mask insertion or removal explicitly wakes its own resident block without a render write, then applies the ordinary boundary-neighbor wake. The neighbor helper alone excludes the center block because ordinary material writes already wake it. Mask changes must not depend on a neighboring material write to resume contact. The current body-coupling path rebuilds masks, so it can wake touched interior body blocks even for stationary bodies; this is confined to that existing footprint. Settled Water can become inactive; render dithering does not wake it. **Current:** a denied slow Mercury pair records the earliest due tick in its source block. The existing `begin_tick` metadata pass wakes due included blocks and clears their deadline. Sleeping blocks therefore progress without a periodic cell scan. Excluded deadlines remain pending; re-entry evaluates only the current modulo lane, with no missed-move catch-up. Clear/replacement discards these deadlines and failed-world quarantine prevents their processing. The [versioned pair policy](granular-interaction-policy.md) owns rate and endpoint rules. **Current, MAT-001 / #158:** `World::schedule_pending_reaction_wake` uses that same earliest block deadline for an eligible compact-pair contact or an Ice thermal contact. It runs after an admitted kernel when the source itself was not written in the current epoch, including successful neighbor-only work. Eligibility uses the existing pair resolver and mask-aware neighbors, independent of the current probability roll. The deadline is strictly in the future, so a missed sample can receive another scheduled opportunity. Waiting does not alter cell content, movement counts or render dirtiness; an inert contact acquires no new deadline. The deadline is shared by all work in a block. Removing one partner does not cancel a deadline that may belong to another source or a transport lane; one already scheduled wake can retire normally after re-evaluation. Interest exclusion, re-entry, clear and failed-world handling use the existing lifecycle above. The bundle's manifest binds all files and the native DLL; `qualification` retains the original automated receipts and graphical captures. **Proposed authoring tree** (final names/schema require #352 review): ```text materials/ schema/material-v1.schema.json registry/identities.json definitions/{legacy,reactive,construction,building}/*.json behaviours/presets.json interactions/{families,pairs,specialized}.json appearances/{recipes,overrides}.json browse/{categories,tags}.json tools/materials/compile_catalogue.py tools/materials/test_catalogue.py ``` Prefer simple JSON plus a deterministic Python-stdlib compiler in v1, because the current repo already maintains portable Python CI tools. Using several author-friendly source files is acceptable **only if** they compile to one validated immutable effective catalogue. The canonical source should contain identity, type, constraints, owned parameters, family memberships, aliases and status. Free-form comments in JSON may be replaced with dedicated `description` fields or adjacent documentation. **Illustrative proposed material record** (not executable today): ```json { "schema_version": 1, "key": "cybersand:wood", "id": 7, "display": {"name": "Wood", "category": "Organics/Wood", "tags": ["timber"]}, "physical": {"phase": "Solid", "density_rank": 720, "hard_surface": true, "granular_support": false}, "behaviour": {"preset": "legacy.wood.v1"}, "appearance": {"rgba8": [116, 78, 48, 255], "recipe": "timber.v1"} } ``` **Generated outputs** should include `material.hpp` descriptors/identity, explicit native capability lookup, compact sparse interaction table/partner sets, stable GDScript IDs and names, picker/browse metadata, RGBA and flair arrays, condition projection and versioned source-derived catalogue manifest. Keep expensive shader algorithms and native kernel implementations hand-coded initially; generate their *metadata*, not a new universal interpreter. **Hard validator gates:** - Stable, non-reused byte IDs; slot 10 remains invalid; `Gas` is a label alias for Smoke=4, not another material ID; reserve/unallocated slots fail cleanly. - Unique keys, names and aliases; valid family references, endpoint/product IDs, kernel enum, radius, state width/meaning, type ranges and support matrix. - Family overlap, duplicate pair, conflicting ordered/unordered matches, cross-rule precedence, invalid supersession, invalid probability representations, uninitiable pair-only definitions and unsupported optional-state contracts fail with understandable source location. - Generate a baseline exact-value oracle from the pinned Current source before replacing hand-authored tables. `--check` regenerates without modifying the tree and fails on drift. Generated files are deterministic, diffable and compatible with repository documentation policies. - Current 132-slot catalogue, all 56 rule identities/indexes/roll cases and 19 specialised mechanisms are identical after the migration. Synthetic new non-hard powder at ID 132 is a compiler-only fixture—not a shipped byte-ID addition—to prove future IDs are not auto-collision-hard. **Intentionally not implemented in v1:** a runtime DSL, hot-loop schema evaluation, user scripts, dynamic pack ID reassignment, or a per-cell behaviour object.
